findings.current: A monster I had seen somewhere before had appeared right in front of me—not in the modern world, but in Murim.
findings.defect: The Korean says this was a monster he had seen many times, not merely once somewhere before. The repeated familiarity supports why he recognizes it immediately.
findings.rationale: 어디선가 많이 봤던 means he had seen it many times somewhere; 많이 is omitted in the assembled English.
findings.replacement: A monster I had seen many times before had appeared right in front of me—not in the modern world, but in Murim.

findings.current: Birds in flight lost their strength and plummeted.
findings.defect: The source specifically depicts birds taking off and then falling as they lose their strength. “In flight” broadens and changes that physical image.
findings.rationale: 날아오르던 새들 refers to birds that were rising/taking flight, not generic birds already in flight.
findings.replacement: Birds taking flight lost their strength and plummeted.

findings.current: His mouth hung open, his eyes bulged wide. Just as his pupils began to roll white beneath the grip of terror—
findings.defect: The current wording says the pupils had already begun turning white. The source places the interruption exactly as they were about to turn white.
findings.rationale: 뒤집히려던 바로 그 순간 means precisely the moment before the pupils turned white, preserving the imminent timing of the intervention.
findings.replacement: His mouth hung open, his eyes bulged wide. Just as his pupils were about to roll white beneath the grip of terror—

summary: The chapter is largely faithful. I found three minor source-fidelity losses involving a repeated-exposure detail and two precise physical-action timings.
